title: Graph Neural Network
description: Deep learning architecture processing graph-structured data via message-passing.
name: Graph Neural Network
summary: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) propagate node features across graph edges via message passing, accumulating neighbor representations to compute node, edge, or graph-level embeddings.
use_when: Analyzing molecular structures, social networks, citation nets, or knowledge graphs.
avoid_when: Working with grid-like or sequential inputs that standard CNNs/transformers model more efficiently.
pros: Natively handles arbitrary graph topologies and relational connections.
Learns translation-invariant features on non-Euclidean domains.
Permutation invariance ensures outputs are independent of node ordering.
cons: Prone to over-smoothing where node representations converge after multiple layers.
Computationally complex to batch efficiently due to irregular graph sizes.
Limited support in standard deep learning serialization libraries.

key_hyperparams.name: aggr
key_hyperparams.note: Neighborhood aggregation method. Common choices are 'sum', 'mean', or 'max'.
